blocks.md:
- Transition elements are found in the centre of the [Periodic Table](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/science/cie/co-ordinated-sciences-double-award/23/chemistry/revision-notes/the-periodic-table/the-periodic-table-and-trends/the-periodic-table/) between Group 2 and Group 3
- Most metals are transition elements and have properties typical of a metal:

  - They are **lustrous**
  - They are **hard** and **strong**
  - They** conduct** heat and electricity
  - They have **high melting points**
  
    - Except mercury: This has a low melting point which is why it is a liquid at room temperature

blocks.text: The transition elements in the Periodic Table

blocks.md: ***Transition elements are found in the middle of the Periodic Table***

- There are some properties that are only typical of transition elements :

  - They form **ions with different charges**
  
    - E.g. Iron forms Fe<sup>2+</sup> and Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions
  - They are useful as **catalysts**
  
    - E.g. Iron is used as the catalyst in the Haber process

- They form **coloured compounds**

  - E.g. Copper forms blue copper sulfate, black copper oxide and green copper carbonate

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Although scandium and zinc are in the transition element area of the Periodic Table, they are not considered transition elements as they do **not** form coloured compounds and have only **one **oxidation state.
